chunks: And from him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'When I enter the Ka'bah, what should I do?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Hold the two rings of the door when you enter, then proceed until you reach the two pillars, so offer prayer upon the red marble. Then, when you exit from the House, and descend from the stairs, offer two cycles of prayer on your right.'

key_terms.الرُّخَامَة الْحَمْرَاء: The red marble, a specific spot inside the Ka'bah where prayer is recommended.
key_terms.الْعَمُودَان: The two pillars, referring to the pillars of the Ka'ah.
key_terms.الْكَعْبَة: The Ka'bah, the cube-shaped building in Mecca that is the focal point of Islamic prayer.
key_terms.حَلْقَتَا الْبَاب: The two rings or handles of the door of the Ka'bah.

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended prayers and actions when entering and exiting the Ka'bah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific Sunnah of visiting the Ka'bah, emphasizing physical engagement with its sacred architecture, such as holding the door rings and praying at the red marble (Hajar al-Hamra). It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of distinguishing between the obligatory Tawaf and these recommended acts of devotion, linking the physical space of the Ka'bah to spiritual elevation. The instruction to pray upon exiting underscores the continuity of worship beyond the circumambulation itself.
